global_summary: The sheet explains whether ASP.NET Core OutputCache should be used for a response, when it is safe, when it is beneficial, how locking prevents or harms cache stampede scenarios, and how OutputCache differs from CDN/browser caching and revalidation behavior.

regions.summary: Safety and benefit gate: avoid caching personal/session/user-specific responses, cookie/session state, side-effect endpoints and non-reusable responses; use OutputCache when the response is safe and reusable.
Usefulness decision road: cache-key reuse/hotness, unused entries, expensive endpoints, large responses, freshness/dynamic data, existing cache layers, and custom server policy.
Locking road: cache stampede prevention, concurrent cache misses, endpoint cost, expiration time, response cost, connection quality, when locking is good/bad and catastrophic locking situations.
Text-heavy OutputCache vs CDN/browser cache road: when redundant, when useful behind CDN, CDN misses, private/internal bypass, app-level cache rules, and revalidation/304 notes.
